condition.purpose: Check the maximum CLTV for a 2-4 Unit property.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review property type and CLTV.
Eligibility Verification: Apply the printed Max CLTV: 80% for a 2-4 Unit property.
Validation and Verification: Compare the recorded CLTV with 80%.
Final Determination: Record whether the maximum CLTV is met.
checks: If SubjectProperty.property_type is 2-4 Units, LoanCore.cltv_percent is no more than 80%.

outcomes.criterion: The property is not 2-4 Units, or CLTV is no more than 80%.
There is no case for this outcome.
The property is 2-4 Units and CLTV is more than 80%.
There is no case for this outcome.

rule.description: Apply the printed maximum CLTV for a 2-4 Unit property.

ledger.clause:
STD-8.1 Eligible property types: SFR, Townhome, PUD, Warrantable Condo, Non-Warrantable Condo, Condotel / PUDtel, 2-4 Units, Manufactured. Restrictions as printed: \[S: Subject Property Type\]

| 2-4 Unit | 80% | 80% | 80% | Printed as “Max CLTV: 80%” with no purpose split |

STD-8.4 Declining market: “-5% CLTV property/borrower full profile” (STD-1.14). \[S: Subject Property Location\]

condition.purpose: Check the Condotel / PUDtel CLTV limit applicable to the transaction.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review property type, transaction purpose, state, and CLTV.
Eligibility Verification: Apply the Condotel / PUDtel cap for the transaction purpose and the printed Florida reduction where applicable.
Validation and Verification: Compare the recorded CLTV with the applicable cap.

checks: If the property is Condotel / PUDtel, CLTV does not exceed 75% for Purchase, 70% for Refi R/T, or 65% for Refi C/O, with -5% CLTV for Florida properties.

The property is Condotel / PUDtel and the applicable CLTV cap, including the printed Florida reduction where applicable, is exceeded.
There is no case for this outcome.

condition.purpose: Review the declining-market CLTV reduction and the requested confirmation about combining it with other caps.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the property and borrower profile and information establishing whether the property is in a declining market.
Eligibility Verification: Apply the stated -5% CLTV property/borrower full profile reduction when the property is in a declining market.
Validation and Verification: Request Acra confirmation on how the reduction combines with other caps.
Final Determination: Record the applicable reduction and whether the requested confirmation has been obtained.
checks: If the property is in a declining market, the -5% CLTV property/borrower full profile reduction is applied.
If the property is in a declining market, Acra confirmation is obtained on how the reduction combines with other caps.

outcomes.criterion: The property is not in a declining market, or the reduction is applied and Acra confirmation on its combination with other caps is obtained.
The property is in a declining market and Acra confirmation on how the reduction combines with other caps is requested but not yet obtained.
The property is in a declining market and the stated reduction is not applied.
The property is not in a declining market.

Property/borrower full profile
Acra confirmation on how the reduction combines with other caps

rule.description: Apply the stated declining-market CLTV reduction and obtain Acra confirmation on how it combines with other caps.

condition.purpose: Determine whether the subject property has an eligible property type.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the subject property's recorded property type.
Eligibility Verification: Compare the property type with the eligible property types in the policy.

STD-8.8 A property is considered listed for sale under §11.5 if it has been listed for sale in the last six months, measured from (a) the last date of being listed to (b) the Application Date. \[G §11.5, p. 12\]

STD-8.9 Loans on such properties will be considered under the following characteristics: the property is not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s); for investment properties, the subject must be occupied by a tenant and may not be vacant; the loan must qualify as either (a) ≥ 1.0 DSCR or (b) 43% maximum DTI (Q-14); a prepayment penalty of at least three (3) years is required unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties; twenty-four (24) months of reserves are required, and cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide; the loan must have a fully amortizing term, interest only is not available; the maximum LTV / CLTV is 65% based on the lesser of (a) appraised value or (b) lowest recent listing price; no subordinate financing is allowed; impounds are required. \[G §11.5, pp. 11–12\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether a vacant property cash-out refinance meets the conditions stated in the Summary.

Eligibility Verification: Apply the stated vacant-property cash-out refinance conditions.
Validation and Verification: Verify each stated condition and request Acra confirmation for loans of $1,500,000 or more and for how the 15 months of ownership are measured.
Final Determination: Record whether the stated conditions are met and whether confirmation remains outstanding.
checks: If the property is vacant and the transaction is a cash-out refinance, the minimum FICO score is 700.
If the property is vacant and the transaction is a cash-out refinance, DSCR is at least 1.15.
If the property is vacant and the transaction is a cash-out refinance, the prepayment penalty is at least three years where allowable.
If the property is vacant and the transaction is a cash-out refinance, no interest-only program is used.
If the property is vacant and the transaction is a cash-out refinance, impounds are in place.
If the property is vacant and the transaction is a cash-out refinance, reserves are at least six months.
If the property is vacant and the transaction is a cash-out refinance with a loan amount under $1,500,000, CLTV is no more than 60%.
If the property is vacant and the transaction is a cash-out refinance, ownership is at least 15 months.
If the property is vacant and the transaction is a cash-out refinance with a loan amount of $1,500,000 or more, Acra confirmation is obtained.

condition.purpose: Determine whether a vacant property rate and term refinance meets the stated requirements in §10.17.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review vacancy, transaction purpose, score, loan amount, CLTV, qualifying DSCR or DTI, prepayment penalty, amortization, impounds, and reserves.
Eligibility Verification: Apply the vacant-property rate and term refinance requirements in §10.17.
Validation and Verification: Verify each requirement and request Acra confirmation for a loan amount exactly $1,000,000 or $2,000,000.
Final Determination: Record whether the requirements are met and whether confirmation remains outstanding.
checks: If the property is vacant and the transaction is a rate and term refinance, the minimum FICO score is 700.
If the property is vacant and the transaction is a rate and term refinance, a loan amount under $1,000,000 has a maximum 70% CLTV.
If the property is vacant and the transaction is a rate and term refinance, a loan amount under $2,000,000 has a maximum 65% CLTV.
If the property is vacant and the transaction is a rate and term refinance, the loan qualifies with minimum 1.000 DSCR or maximum 40.0% DTI.
If the property is vacant and the transaction is a rate and term refinance, the prepayment penalty is at least two years where allowable.
If the property is vacant and the transaction is a rate and term refinance, full amortization is used and no interest-only program is used.
If the property is vacant and the transaction is a rate and term refinance, impounds are in place.
If the property is vacant and the transaction is a rate and term refinance, reserves are at least six months.
If the property is vacant and the transaction is a rate and term refinance with a loan amount exactly $1,000,000 or $2,000,000, Acra confirmation is obtained.

outcomes.criterion: The property is not vacant or the transaction is not a rate and term refinance, or every applicable requirement is met and any required Acra confirmation is obtained.
A loan amount exactly $1,000,000 or $2,000,000 requires Acra confirmation that has been requested but not obtained.
The property is vacant, the transaction is a rate and term refinance, and any applicable requirement is not met.
The property is not vacant or the transaction is not a rate and term refinance.

STD-1.10 Minimum loan amount \$100,000; maximum loan amount \$3,000,000; loan amount to be in \$50 increments. \[S: Loan Amount\]

STD-1.11 Seller concession / other contributions: limited to 3% of the sale price. \[S: Loan Amount\]

STD-1.12 Gifting is allowed and “requires borrower to contribute a minimum of 10% of the purchase price consisting of their own funds”; §8.7 states the contribution as the applicant's “own sourced and seasoned funds”. Gift documentation requirements are in the Seller's Guide gift-fund section, not reproduced (Appendix B). \[S: Loan Amount; G §8.7, p. 12\]

STD-9.1 Gift funds, investment property or second homes: applicant(s) are required to contribute a portion of their own sourced and seasoned funds to the transaction at a minimum of 10% of the purchase price. Gift documentation requirements are in the Seller's Guide gift-fund section (Appendix B). \[G §8.7, p. 12; S: Loan Amount\]

STD-9.2 Verification of the seasoning of funds to close is required on loans over 70% CLTV for consumer transactions, or business purpose loans where funds to close are over \$50,000 and over 70% CLTV. Whether any loan on this program is a consumer transaction: Acra confirmation requested → Q-27. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.3 Where the account(s) serving as the source of funds must be verified, verification may include a copy of the borrower's bank statement(s) for the most recent month(s), or a VOD reflecting a current and average balance for the most recent month(s). \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.4 “All transactions require a minimum of 30-days documentation.” Whether any seasoning period applies to domestic funds beyond this documentation minimum: Acra confirmation requested → Q-12. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.5 “In contrast to the above, but consistent with §3.10.1 of this Guide, funds held in a foreign bank / currency will need to be repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing and Foreign Nationals, regardless of LTV / CLTV, need to document a minimum of 60 days seasoning.” Whether the repatriation requirement applies to any borrower holding funds abroad or only to foreign nationals, and what evidence applies: Acra confirmation requested → Q-12. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the stated STD-9.5 requirements for foreign funds and Foreign Nationals are met.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review available evidence about the location and currency of funds, seasoning, and any transfer to the closing account.

Eligibility Verification: Establish whether funds are held in a foreign bank / currency and whether the borrower is a Foreign National; note that the source requests confirmation about the scope of the repatriation requirement and applicable evidence.

Validation and Verification: For Foreign Nationals, verify a minimum of 60 days seasoning regardless of LTV / CLTV. Verify that foreign bank / currency funds are repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing, subject to the source's unresolved scope question.
Final Determination: Determine whether the applicable stated requirements are documented.
checks: Foreign Nationals document a minimum of 60 days seasoning, regardless of LTV / CLTV.
Funds held in a foreign bank / currency are repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing, where the repatriation requirement applies.

outcomes.criterion: The applicable seasoning and repatriation requirements are met and documented.
Applicability of the repatriation requirement or the evidence that applies remains subject to the requested Acra confirmation.
An applicable stated seasoning or repatriation requirement is not met.
Neither foreign funds nor a Foreign National condition applies.

STD-9.6 The sources state reserves only for the situations below, and state the payment basis only where shown. The base requirement where no trigger applies, the payment basis where only “months” is stated, permitted sources, whether overlapping triggers are cumulative, and whether reserves substituted for rent loss insurance are additional: Acra confirmation requested → Q-07. \[S; G\]

| **Trigger** | **Reserves as printed** | **Source** |
|----|----|----|
| LTV \> 80.00% | 6 months PITIA reserves | S: Income Documentation |
| FICO \< 620 | 12 Months | S: Credit Requirements |
| First-time homebuyer | Minimum six months reserves (“Requires 6mos Reserves”) | G §3.13; S: Restrictions |
| Vacant property — rate & term refinance | Minimum six months reserves | G §10.17; S: Occupancy Type |
| Vacant property — cash-out refinance | 6 months reserves | S: Occupancy Type |
| Property listed for sale within six months | Twenty-four (24) months of reserves; cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide | G §11.5 |
| Forbearance or mortgage lates in the last 12 months, tenant-occupied subject, without timely receipt of the prior two months' rent | 12 months of the subject's payment in reserve, which may be from the transaction's cash-in-hand | G §5.32 |
| Rent loss insurance required but cannot be obtained | Two (2) months reserves for every one (1) month of coverage not provided | G §23.40 |

6.1 Entity eligibility and guarantees
STD-6.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

ledger.clause:
6.1 Entity eligibility and guarantees
STD-6.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the required entity documentation has been provided and meets the stated requirements.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the entity documents provided, including formation documents and amendments; the Operating Agreement or Bylaws and referenced exhibits; ownership evidence; applicable stock certificates, stock ledger, Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate, K-1 statements and CPA or Tax Preparer letter; identification; good-standing and qualification documents; EIN or TIN evidence; unanimous written consent or board resolution; and any required Power of Attorney.

Eligibility Verification: Verify that the formation documents and amendments and the applicable Operating Agreement or Bylaws are complete and legible, include all referenced exhibits, address management, borrowing and contracting authorization, and identify authorized signers. Verify that ownership interests are evidenced as required, and that corporate share evidence accounts for all outstanding shares, including those held by the corporation.

Validation and Verification: Verify that entity names match identification or that a letter of explanation addresses any discrepancy; that the Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent is valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date; that any required qualification to operate in the applicable state is provided; and that IRS Form SS4 or Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter is provided. Verify the required unanimous written consent or board resolution is signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest, authorizes the transaction with Acra Lending, and identifies who is authorized to sign and bind the entity. Verify that any Power of Attorney used to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee is utilized by the principal. Do not accept borrower letters stating that required documents are not required, available, or excused.

Final Determination: Record whether all applicable required documents have been provided and meet the stated requirements; note that Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.
checks: The complete, legible Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments thereto are provided.

The complete, legible Operating Agreement for LLCs and Partnerships, or Bylaws for corporations, with all referenced exhibits and amendments, is provided and states whether the entity is member or manager managed, contains authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers.

All required documentation evidencing ownership interests is provided, including the applicable ownership names and interests or membership interest certificates / units in compliance with the Operating Agreement.

For S or C Corporations, required shareholder / stockholder certificates or, if stock certificates are lost or unavailable, the stock ledger is provided and accounts for all outstanding shares noted in the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization, including those held by the corporation; an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate is provided if stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable.

For S-corporations or Partnerships where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable, the most recent preceding tax year's K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest and a letter from the CPA or Tax Preparer affirming current ownership interest are provided, with a statement to that effect if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed.
Names on the entity documents match the identification or a letter of explanation addresses the discrepancy.
A Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date is provided.

A Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted is provided if the entity is formed in a state other than where business is performed or where the property is located.

IRS Form SS4 or Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter is provided, unless an EIN exception request is submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds.

A Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest authorizes the transaction with Acra Lending and identifies who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity.
Any Power of Attorney used to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee is utilized by the principal.
No borrower letter is relied on to claim a required document is not required, available, or excused.

An applicable required-document check is not met, or a borrower letter is relied on in place of a required document.
The borrower is not an entity borrower.

6.2 Entity documentation
STD-6.10 The documents below are required, without exception, and borrower letters stating that they are not required, available, or excused from providing such documents are not acceptable. \[G §3.12, pp. 8–9\]

- Complete, legible copy of the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments thereto.

- Complete (with all referenced exhibits), legible copy of the Operating Agreement for LLCs and Partnerships, or Bylaws for corporations, and all amendments, that states whether the entity is member or manager managed, contains authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers. Additional information may be required if the formation documents and the Operating Agreement or Bylaws conflict.

- All documentation evidencing ownership interests: for LLCs and Partnerships, the Operating Agreement must identify, or attach as an exhibit, all persons by name with their ownership interest, or provide copies of the membership interest certificates / units in compliance with the Operating Agreement.

- For S or C Corporations: shareholder / stockholder certificates that comply with the Bylaws, if any, or, if stock certificates are lost or unavailable, the corporation's stock ledger. The certificate or ledger must account for all outstanding shares noted in the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization, including those held by the corporation. If stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable, an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate is required.

- For S-corporations or Partnerships, where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable: (i) the most recent preceding tax year's K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest, and (ii) a letter from the CPA or Tax Preparer affirming current ownership interest, with a statement to that effect if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed.

6.2 Entity documentation
- Names on the entity documents must match the identification; if they do not match exactly, a letter of explanation is required to address the discrepancy.

- Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date.

- Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted, if the entity is formed in a state other than where business is performed or where the property is located.

- IRS Form SS4 or Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter for the entity. EIN exception requests may be submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds.

- A Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest, (i) authorizing the transaction with Acra Lending and (ii) identifying who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity. It may be required by the Operating Agreement or Bylaws even where ownership is held by one individual. It cannot be used to designate a signor on a personal guarantee, only an authorized signor for the loan documents signed by the entity.

- A Power of Attorney must be utilized by the principal to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee; see §23.5(C), not reproduced (Appendix B).

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

condition.purpose: Determine whether title may be vested in the inter vivos revocable trust under the stated requirements.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the trust or Certification of Trust, title commitment, and any written exception by Acra Senior Management.

Eligibility Verification: Verify that the Trust is valid under the laws of the state in which it is established; is revocable during a Trustor's lifetime; is established by one or more natural persons and became effective during their lifetime; and has the individual(s) establishing the Trust as its primary beneficiary.

Validation and Verification: Verify that the Trust or Certification of Trust provides all listed trust information; that the Trustee has power to hold title and mortgage the property; that beneficiary written consent is not required or has been granted in writing for the mortgage; and that there is no unusual risk or impairment to the lender's rights and title in the Trust does not diminish the lender's rights as a creditor. Verify that written exception by Acra Senior Management is obtained if the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same. Do not treat an irrevocable trust as permitted.

Final Determination: Record whether each trust vesting requirement is met; note that Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.
checks: A complete, legible copy of the Trust or a Certification of Trust states the existence and date of the Trust; Trustor(s) and current Trustee(s); Trustee powers; whether the Trust is revocable and, if revocable, who holds the right to revoke; required signing Trustees; the Trust identification number; how title to Trust assets should be taken; and that the Trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner.
The Trust is valid under the laws of the state in which it is established and is revocable, meaning it can be changed or canceled at any time for any reason during a Trustor's lifetime.

The Trust is established by one or more natural persons, solely or jointly, and becomes effective during the lifetime of the person(s) establishing it; the primary beneficiary is the individual(s) establishing the Trust.
Written exception by Acra Senior Management is obtained if the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same.

The Trust specifies that the Trustee has the power to hold title and mortgage the property; that beneficiary written consent is not needed or has been granted in writing for the mortgage; that there is no unusual risk or impairment to the lender's rights; and that holding title in the Trust does not diminish the lender's rights as a creditor.
The Trust is not an irrevocable trust.

STD-6.13 Title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust is permitted when all of the following requirements are followed. \[G §3.12, pp. 9–10\]

- A complete, legible copy of the Trust, or a Certification of Trust stating: the existence and date of the Trust; the Trustor(s) and the current Trustee(s); the powers of the Trustee; whether the Trust is revocable and, if revocable, who holds the right to revoke; the names and number of the Trustees required to sign on behalf of the Trust; the Trust identification number (a Social Security number or an IRS-issued Tax Identification Number); how title to the Trust assets should be taken; and a statement that the Trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner.

- The Trust must be valid under the laws of the state in which it is established.

- The Trust must be revocable, meaning it can be changed or canceled at any time for any reason during a Trustor's lifetime. Irrevocable trust is not permitted.

- The Trust must be established by one or more natural persons, solely or jointly (Grantor, Trustor, or Settlor), and must become effective during the lifetime of the person(s) establishing it.

- The primary beneficiary of the Trust must be the individual(s) establishing the Trust.

- Written exception by Acra Senior Management must be obtained if the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same.

- The Trust must specify that the Trustee has the power to hold title and mortgage the property; that the beneficiary does not need to grant written consent for the Trust to borrow money, or that such consent has been granted in writing for purposes of the mortgage; that there is no unusual risk or impairment to the lender's rights; and that holding title in the Trust does not diminish the lender's rights as a creditor.

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

6.1 Entity eligibility and guarantees
STD-6.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether a borrower with bankruptcy or foreclosure meets the printed seasoning-based maximum CLTV restriction.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the credit report and case record for bankruptcy or foreclosure, seasoning, loan purpose, and CLTV.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Determine whether the borrower has bankruptcy or foreclosure and identify the seasoning as printed.
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Apply the printed maximum CLTV for the applicable seasoning and purpose: ≥ 36 Mo, 24-35 Mo, 12-23 Mo, or < 12 Mo.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Determine whether the applicable restriction is met.
checks: If seasoning is ≥ 36 Mo, there are No Restrictions.
If seasoning is 24-35 Mo, CLTV does not exceed 80% for Purchase or 75% for Refi R/T, Refi C/O.
If seasoning is 12-23 Mo, CLTV does not exceed 65% for Purchase or 65% for Refi R/T, Refi C/O.
If seasoning is < 12 Mo, the case is Ineligible.

condition.purpose: Determine whether the applicant meets the stated score and tradeline requirements and, where applicable, the stated overlay.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the credit report for reported score count, tradelines, and credit history.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Determine whether the applicant has scores from 3 repositories, 2 or fewer scores, or 1 or No Score / Deficient Tradelines.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: For 2 or fewer scores, verify either 2 tradelines & 24 month history, or 3 tradelines & 12 month history. For 1 or No Score / Deficient Tradelines, verify each of the three entries as printed: Max 65% LTV/CLTV; DSCR Ratio ≥ 1.1; 24mos 0x30 housing history.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Determine whether the applicable score and tradeline requirements are met.
checks: If the applicant has scores from 3 repositories, the score-count requirement is met with no tradeline overlay.
If the applicant has 2 or fewer scores, the applicant has either 2 tradelines & 24 month history, or 3 tradelines & 12 month history.
If the applicant has 1 or No Score / Deficient Tradelines, CLTV does not exceed 65%.
If the applicant has 1 or No Score / Deficient Tradelines, DSCR Ratio is ≥ 1.1.
If the applicant has 1 or No Score / Deficient Tradelines, the applicant has 24mos 0x30 housing history.

outcomes.criterion: The applicable score and tradeline requirements are met, including all applicable entries for 1 or No Score / Deficient Tradelines.
There is no case for this outcome.
An applicable score or tradeline requirement is not met.
There is no case for this outcome.

The DSCR Ratio.
Whether the applicant has 24mos 0x30 housing history.

condition.purpose: Determine whether a borrower with a short sale, deed-in-lieu, or modification meets the printed seasoning-based maximum CLTV restriction.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the credit report and case record for short sale, deed-in-lieu, or modification, seasoning, loan purpose, and CLTV.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Determine whether the borrower has a short sale, deed-in-lieu, or modification and identify the seasoning as printed.
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Apply the printed maximum CLTV for the applicable seasoning and purpose: ≥ 24 Mo, 12-23 Mo, or < 12 Mo.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Determine whether the applicable restriction is met.
checks: If seasoning is ≥ 24 Mo, there are No Restrictions.
If seasoning is 12-23 Mo, CLTV does not exceed 80% for Purchase or 75% for Refi R/T, Refi C/O.
If seasoning is < 12 Mo, CLTV does not exceed 75% for Purchase or 70% for Refi R/T, Refi C/O.

outcomes.criterion: The borrower has no short sale, deed-in-lieu, or modification, or the applicable printed seasoning restriction is met.
There is no case for this outcome.
The borrower has a short sale, deed-in-lieu, or modification and exceeds the applicable maximum CLTV.
There is no case for this outcome.

rule.description: Apply the printed short sale, deed-in-lieu, and modification seasoning and CLTV restrictions.

ledger.clause:
4.1 Citizenship types and limits
STD-4.1 Eligible borrower citizenship types: US Citizen, Permanent Resident, Non-Permanent Resident, Foreign National, ITIN. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.2 Permanent Resident must have an unexpired PRA ID and SSA card / SSA-89. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.3 Non-Permanent Resident must have proof of legal residency, which may include an unexpired employment authorization document (EAD) or valid visa. Limit printed as “Max Loan Amount: \$1.5M: Max CLTV 80%” — whether this is two independent limits or one conditional limit: Acra confirmation requested → Q-21. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.4 Foreign National: “Borrowers whose Primary Residence is not located in the United States of America.” Maximum CLTV 70% (purchase) and 65% (refinance — rate & term and cash-out); “Price loan at FICO equal to 700”. No maximum loan amount is stated for foreign nationals: Acra confirmation requested → Q-21. Program documentation is in section 5. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.5 ITIN: “ITIN is defined as any non-resident that is unable to provide any of the ‘Non-Permanent Resident Alien’ documents listed above.” Maximum loan amount \$1.0M; minimum FICO 640; maximum CLTV by FICO as printed below. §3.10 separately admits ITIN holders under the foreign-national program when they reside outside the US. Whether a US-resident ITIN holder is eligible, and whether the tier printed “FICO 700” means 700 and above: Acra confirmation requested → Q-03. \[S: Borrower Citizenship; G §3.10, p. 6\]

| **ITIN tier as printed** | **Purchase** | **Refinance — R/T and cash-out** |
|--------------------------|--------------|----------------------------------|
| “FICO 700”               | 70%          | 65%                              |
| “FICO 660 to 699”        | 65%          | 60%                              |
| “FICO 640 to 659”        | 60%          | 60%                              |

condition.purpose: Verify foreign-account funds and the stated documentation and timing conditions for funds to close.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: For assets held / foreign accounts, obtain a copy of the two (2) most recent statements of that account. Review any required letter of explanation, sixty (60) day chain of funds, and English translations.

Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Verify funds in U.S. Dollar equivalency at the current exchange rate via www.xe.com or the Wall Street Journal conversion table. Verify a minimum of 60 days seasoning regardless of LTV / CLTV. If funds are not seasoned a minimum of sixty (60) days, require a letter of explanation along with information to comprise a sixty (60) day chain of funds. Verify that sufficient funds to close are on deposit with the Escrow / Closing Agent at least three (3) business days (including Saturdays for this calculation) prior to any closing date, and that funds held in a foreign bank / currency are repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Translate into English bank statements in any language other than English. Validate the exchange-rate conversion, statements, seasoning, chain of funds if required, deposit timing, and repatriation timing.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the foreign-account funds meet the stated verification, documentation, and timing requirements.
checks: Foreign-account assets are verified in U.S. Dollar equivalency at the current exchange rate via www.xe.com or the Wall Street Journal conversion table.
A copy of the two (2) most recent statements of the account is provided.

Funds are documented with a minimum of 60 days seasoning, regardless of LTV / CLTV; if funds are not seasoned a minimum of sixty (60) days, a letter of explanation and information to comprise a sixty (60) day chain of funds are provided.
Sufficient funds to close are on deposit with the Escrow / Closing Agent at least three (3) business days (including Saturdays for this calculation) prior to any closing date.
Funds held in a foreign bank / currency are repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing.
Bank statements in any language other than English are translated into English.

outcomes.criterion: All applicable foreign-account verification, documentation, seasoning, deposit, repatriation, and translation requirements are met.
A required statement, conversion, translation, seasoning record, chain of funds, deposit, or repatriation item remains outstanding.
An applicable foreign-account requirement is not met.
The applicant has no assets held / foreign accounts subject to these requirements.

missing_reads: Current exchange rate and the resulting U.S. Dollar equivalency; the two most recent account statements; seasoning duration; if seasoning is less than sixty (60) days, the letter of explanation and information comprising the sixty (60) day chain of funds; funds-on-deposit date, closing date, and sufficiency of funds to close; repatriation date; statement language and English translation where needed.

rule.description: Verify foreign-account funds in U.S. Dollar equivalency and review the required account statements, seasoning, transfer timing, and translations.

STD-5.1 Foreign Nationals are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions only (i.e. investment properties). \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.2 Eligible under the Foreign National Program are Non-Resident Aliens who are not authorized to live or work in the U.S. “A true Foreign National may periodically visit the U.S. for various reasons including vacation and / or business, may purchase property for limited personal use or investment, or may own a U.S based business entity, but they must reside outside of the U.S.” \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.3 Borrowers who are holders of Individual Tax Identification Numbers (ITIN) are eligible for this program if they reside outside of the U.S. \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.4 “Due to market exchange rates, applicants are to be reviewed with scrutiny toward a post-close financial position and their ability to mitigate exchange rate fluctuations.” \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.5 “See 3.10 for OFAC restrictions and state specific exclusions” — not reproduced (Appendix B). \[G §3.10, p. 7\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether a Foreign National borrower meets the stated Foreign National Program eligibility conditions, including the stated ITIN pathway.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review information establishing the transaction purpose, the borrower’s residence, and whether the borrower is authorized to live or work in the U.S.

Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Verify that the transaction is business purpose (i.e. investment property). Verify that a Foreign National Program borrower is a Non-Resident Alien who is not authorized to live or work in the U.S. and resides outside of the U.S. For an ITIN holder relying on this program, verify that the holder resides outside of the U.S.
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Validate the reviewed purpose and residence information and the borrower’s authorization status.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the applicable Foreign National Program conditions are met.
checks: A Foreign National’s transaction is business purpose (i.e. an investment property).
A borrower qualifying as a Foreign National Program Non-Resident Alien resides outside of the U.S. and is not authorized to live or work in the U.S.
An ITIN holder relying on the Foreign National Program resides outside of the U.S.

outcomes.criterion: The applicable Foreign National or ITIN-holder conditions are verified as met.
A required purpose, residence, or authorization fact has not yet been established.
An applicable Foreign National or ITIN-holder condition is not met.
The borrower is not being considered under the Foreign National Program and is not an ITIN holder relying on that program.

ledger.clause:
4.1 Citizenship types and limits
STD-4.1 Eligible borrower citizenship types: US Citizen, Permanent Resident, Non-Permanent Resident, Foreign National, ITIN. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.2 Permanent Resident must have an unexpired PRA ID and SSA card / SSA-89. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.3 Non-Permanent Resident must have proof of legal residency, which may include an unexpired employment authorization document (EAD) or valid visa. Limit printed as “Max Loan Amount: \$1.5M: Max CLTV 80%” — whether this is two independent limits or one conditional limit: Acra confirmation requested → Q-21. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.4 Foreign National: “Borrowers whose Primary Residence is not located in the United States of America.” Maximum CLTV 70% (purchase) and 65% (refinance — rate & term and cash-out); “Price loan at FICO equal to 700”. No maximum loan amount is stated for foreign nationals: Acra confirmation requested → Q-21. Program documentation is in section 5. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.5 ITIN: “ITIN is defined as any non-resident that is unable to provide any of the ‘Non-Permanent Resident Alien’ documents listed above.” Maximum loan amount \$1.0M; minimum FICO 640; maximum CLTV by FICO as printed below. §3.10 separately admits ITIN holders under the foreign-national program when they reside outside the US. Whether a US-resident ITIN holder is eligible, and whether the tier printed “FICO 700” means 700 and above: Acra confirmation requested → Q-03. \[S: Borrower Citizenship; G §3.10, p. 6\]

| **ITIN tier as printed** | **Purchase** | **Refinance — R/T and cash-out** |
|--------------------------|--------------|----------------------------------|
| “FICO 700”               | 70%          | 65%                              |
| “FICO 660 to 699”        | 65%          | 60%                              |
| “FICO 640 to 659”        | 60%          | 60%                              |

condition.purpose: Apply the stated ITIN limits without resolving the source’s unanswered eligibility and FICO-tier questions by assumption.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: For an ITIN borrower, review loan amount, FICO, transaction purpose, and CLTV.

Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Apply maximum loan amount $1.0M and minimum FICO 640. Apply the printed CLTV tiers: “FICO 700” — 70% purchase and 65% refinance — R/T and cash-out; “FICO 660 to 699” — 65% purchase and 60% refinance — R/T and cash-out; “FICO 640 to 659” — 60% purchase and 60% refinance — R/T and cash-out.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Obtain Acra confirmation under Q-03 on whether a US-resident ITIN holder is eligible and whether the tier printed “FICO 700” means 700 and above. Do not assume an answer to either question.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record the applicable stated limits and whether the requested clarifications have been obtained.
checks: The ITIN loan amount is no more than $1.0M.
The ITIN borrower’s FICO is at least 640.
The applicable printed ITIN CLTV tier is met, without treating “FICO 700” as 700 and above unless Acra confirms that interpretation.
Acra confirmation under Q-03 has resolved whether a US-resident ITIN holder is eligible.

outcomes.criterion: The ITIN limits applicable under the confirmed interpretation are met and the required Q-03 eligibility clarification has been obtained.
The borrower is an ITIN holder and Q-03 clarification is outstanding, or an applicable tier or eligibility fact remains unresolved.
An applicable stated ITIN loan amount, minimum FICO, or CLTV limit is not met.
The borrower is not an ITIN holder.

missing_reads: Acra confirmation under Q-03; the transaction purpose and applicable printed FICO tier; confirmation whether “FICO 700” means 700 and above.

rule.description: Verify the stated ITIN loan amount, minimum FICO, and applicable CLTV terms while preserving the requested clarification.

condition.purpose: Determine whether the stated documentation requirements for actual rents exceeding market rents are met, without resolving which rent controls qualification.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the lease_agreement and bank_statement for lease terms and rental income receipt.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Determine whether actual rents exceed market rents.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Verify two (2) consecutive months proof of rental income receipt and lease agreement(s) to continue at a minimum of three (3) months after closing. Verify that the rents are not prepaid and that security deposits are not counted towards receipt.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Determine whether the stated documentation and receipt conditions are met.
checks: When actual rents exceed market rents, two (2) consecutive months proof of rental income receipt and lease agreement(s) to continue at a minimum of three (3) months after closing are documented, rents are not prepaid, and security deposits are not counted towards receipt.

ledger.clause:
STD-3.5 Formula: the lesser of annual in-place rent or market rent (STD-3.1). \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

STD-3.6 Note in the same section: “Acra may use the higher of actual or market rents. Where actual rents exceed market rents, then evidence of actual rents must be documented via two (2) consecutive months proof of rental income receipt and lease agreement(s) to continue at a minimum of three (3) months after closing. Note: Security Deposit does not count towards receipt, and the rents cannot be prepaid.” \[G §5.32, p. 3; repeated under Actual Rents, p. 5\]

STD-3.7 This document does not select between STD-3.5 and STD-3.6. When market rent may be used if actual rent is lower, when higher actual rent may be used, and whether the stated documentation is sufficient or further approval is required: Acra confirmation requested → Q-01.

STD-3.8 “If vacant property is being purchased, qualifying rents are taken from the 1007 or 1025 Appraisal report, as applicable, for qualifying income.” Rental income from the purchase of a vacant property requires a 1007 survey if it is the subject of an Acra loan. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §5.30–5.31, p. 4\]

condition.purpose: Determine the DSCR using the lesser of annual in-place rent or market rent over annual PITIA, including subordinate financing in the denominator.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the appraisal_report and lease_agreement for market rent and in-place rent information, and review available loan information for PITIA and subordinate financing.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Determine whether DSCR is to be calculated; No Ratio DSCR does not calculate a DSCR.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Use the lesser of annual in-place rent or market rent as the numerator. Use annual principal, interest, real estate taxes, property insurance, homeowner's / condominium association fees, and subordinate financing, if applicable, as the denominator. Use the first payment due under the Note.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Calculate and record the DSCR. Do not resolve the interest-only payment question or the rent-selection conflict beyond the stated formula.
checks: The calculated DSCR equals the lesser of annual in-place rent or market rent divided by annual PITIA, including subordinate financing, if applicable, using the first payment due under the Note.

ledger.clause:
STD-3.1 “Acra calculates the DSCR by dividing (a) the lesser of (i) annual in-place rent or (ii) market rent (reference §14.14) by (b) the sum of annual principal, interest, real estate taxes, property insurance, and homeowner's / condominium association fees (collectively, ‘PITIA’). Subordinate financing, if applicable, would also be included in the denominator for the sake of this calculation.” \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

STD-3.2 “Acra calculates the DSCR utilizing the first payment due under the terms of the Note.” §7.5 defines Interest Only payments as “the amount sufficient to pay the accrued interest to the mortgage on a monthly basis at the time of origination”, while the §5.32 denominator lists “annual principal, interest …”. Which payment enters the DSCR denominator on an interest-only loan: Acra confirmation requested → Q-26. \[G §7.5, p. 13; §5.32, p. 3\]

STD-3.3 The reference to subordinate financing in the denominator is a calculation rule; it does not itself establish that a subordinate lien is permitted. Whether and when subordinate financing is permitted: Acra confirmation requested → Q-18. \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

STD-3.4 §14.14 (market rent), referenced in the formula, is not reproduced in the excerpt (Appendix B). \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

STD-3.5 Formula: the lesser of annual in-place rent or market rent (STD-3.1). \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

STD-3.6 Note in the same section: “Acra may use the higher of actual or market rents. Where actual rents exceed market rents, then evidence of actual rents must be documented via two (2) consecutive months proof of rental income receipt and lease agreement(s) to continue at a minimum of three (3) months after closing. Note: Security Deposit does not count towards receipt, and the rents cannot be prepaid.” \[G §5.32, p. 3; repeated under Actual Rents, p. 5\]

STD-3.7 This document does not select between STD-3.5 and STD-3.6. When market rent may be used if actual rent is lower, when higher actual rent may be used, and whether the stated documentation is sufficient or further approval is required: Acra confirmation requested → Q-01.

STD-3.8 “If vacant property is being purchased, qualifying rents are taken from the 1007 or 1025 Appraisal report, as applicable, for qualifying income.” Rental income from the purchase of a vacant property requires a 1007 survey if it is the subject of an Acra loan. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §5.30–5.31, p. 4\]

STD-3.19 “File can qualify without calculating a DSCR Ratio to a maximum LTV / CLTV as described on the appropriate program matrix depending on FICO and other requirement. Requires 1007; however, DSCR is not calculated.” The Summary's No Ratio caps and minimum FICO are STD-3.17. \[G §5.33, p. 3; S: Income Documentation\]

STD-3.20 “Proof of actual rents is not required. Property may be short-term rental or long-term rental (appropriate pricing applies).” \[G §5.33, p. 3\]

STD-3.21 Whether No Ratio is available where another condition carries its own minimum DSCR (STD-3.16 and the table above): Acra confirmation requested → Q-13. Whether the short-term-rental caps apply to a No Ratio file: Acra confirmation requested → Q-02.

STD-3.22 Rent loss insurance applies to No Ratio DSCR (STD-8.12). \[G §23.40, p. 13\]

STD-1.7 “A 1007 will always be required on DSCR transactions – for avoidance of doubt, even on No Ratio DSCR”. Whether a Form 1025 satisfies this for a 2-4 unit property: Acra confirmation requested → Q-08. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-1.8 All borrowers purchasing or refinancing a one- to four-family investment property must execute a One- to Four-Family Rider with the loan documents and provide rent loss insurance coverage per §23.40 (STD-8.11 to 8.14). \[G §3.41, p. 11\]

STD-1.9 Only the subject property, principal residence and second homes are required to be listed on the application or Schedule of Real Estate Owned. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §4.15, p. 5\]

STD-3.9 Acra requires the Single-Family Comparable Rent Schedule (FNMA Form 1007) for single family properties on (i) all DSCR qualifying files, (ii) lease-option purchase transactions where the down payment required in §3.45 is generated from excess monthly rent contributions, or (iii) when proposed rental income is being used to qualify. \[G §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-3.10 A 1007 may be from the original appraiser or any state licensed appraiser. \[G §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-3.11 Single family investment properties with excessive monthly rent payments reflected on the lease require documentation supporting that the monthly rent is typical for the area; acceptable documentation may include classified ads from local newspapers, a 1007 completed by the appraiser, or a market rent survey completed by a local real estate company or rental management company familiar with the market rents in the area. \[G §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-3.12 Short-term rental, appraisal form: for properties occupied as a short-term rental, an STRpro or similar appraisal form is acceptable as replacement to a 1007 as long as it is signed by an appropriately licensed appraiser. \[G §14.13, p. 4\]

3.3 Rent schedules and rent evidence
STD-3.9 Acra requires the Single-Family Comparable Rent Schedule (FNMA Form 1007) for single family properties on (i) all DSCR qualifying files, (ii) lease-option purchase transactions where the down payment required in §3.45 is generated from excess monthly rent contributions, or (iii) when proposed rental income is being used to qualify. \[G §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-3.10 A 1007 may be from the original appraiser or any state licensed appraiser. \[G §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-3.11 Single family investment properties with excessive monthly rent payments reflected on the lease require documentation supporting that the monthly rent is typical for the area; acceptable documentation may include classified ads from local newspapers, a 1007 completed by the appraiser, or a market rent survey completed by a local real estate company or rental management company familiar with the market rents in the area. \[G §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-3.12 Short-term rental, appraisal form: for properties occupied as a short-term rental, an STRpro or similar appraisal form is acceptable as replacement to a 1007 as long as it is signed by an appropriately licensed appraiser. \[G §14.13, p. 4\]

STD-3.13 Short-term rental, actual rents: “Acra can accept short term rentals with 12-month ledgers from condotel management companies, property managers, AirBnB, VRBO, etcetera as documentation for actual rents.” How a 12-month ledger establishes qualifying rent, and how the receipt and lease conditions of STD-3.6 apply to short-term rentals: Acra confirmation requested → Q-02. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §14.13, p. 4\]

STD-3.14 Short-term rental caps: “Properties qualifying with short-term rentals are limited to 75% & 70% LTV / CLTV for Purchase or Refinance transactions respectively”; the Summary states maximum CLTV 75% (purchase) and 70% (refinance — rate & term and cash-out), minimum FICO 640. \[G §5.32, p. 3; S: Occupancy Type\]

STD-4.9 “Acra defines a First Time Home Buyers (‘FTHB’) as an application where all Applicants have never previously owned a home (real property).” \[G §3.13, p. 10\]

STD-4.10 DSCR: Acra allows first-time homebuyers under all of the following: minimum 700 FICO score; maximum 70% CLTV; minimum DSCR of 1.150; maximum loan amount of \$1,000,000; full amortization required, no interest-only programs; impounds required; minimum six months reserves. STD-4.11 “Where a FTHB is purchasing an Investment property and the loan is qualifying via DTI program, the maximum DTI will be 43.0%.” Noted as a DTI-program provision — Q-14. \[G §3.13, p. 10\]

STD-4.12 §3.12 separately requires at least one guarantor with prior homeownership experience where the borrower is an entity (STD-6.9). How that requirement and the first-time-homebuyer allowance interact: Acra confirmation requested → Q-09.

rule.description: Determine whether a stated first-time homebuyer, vacant-property refinance, or listed-for-sale exclusion bars an interest-only loan.

ledger.clause:
STD-10.3 Interest Only, 5 Yr / 30 Year Fixed or 5/1 and 7/1 ARM: minimum loan ≥ \$250K; minimum 640 credit score. \[S: Product Requirements\]

STD-10.4 Interest Only, 10 Yr / 40 Year Term: minimum loan ≥ \$250K; minimum 640 credit score; maximum 80% LTV / CLTV; maximum \$3M loan amount. \[S: Product Requirements\]

STD-10.5 Interest-only is not available to first-time homebuyers (STD-4.10), on vacant-property refinances (STD-8.6 and 8.7) or on properties listed for sale (STD-8.9). \[G §3.13, §10.17, §11.5\]

STD-10.6 Interest Only payments are calculated as the amount sufficient to pay the accrued interest on the mortgage monthly at the time of origination, usually for a set term at the beginning of the repayment term; after that term the payments are recast to a fully amortized payment for the balance of the term ending at maturity. Acra calculates the DSCR using the first payment due under the Note (STD-3.2; which payment enters the denominator on an interest-only loan is Q-26). The excerpt's DTI calculation for interest-only loans (first fully amortized payment on the original balance; for an ARM, the highest achievable rate at that payment's due date) is a DTI-program provision — Q-14. \[G §7.5, p. 13\]

Final Determination: Record whether the subject property meets the definition of investment property.

rule.description: Determine whether the subject property satisfies the program's investment-property occupancy requirement.

ledger.clause:
1.1 Occupancy, purpose and qualification
STD-1.1 Occupancy is investment property (non-owner occupied) only. \[S: Occupancy Type\]

STD-1.2 An investment property is “a one- to four-unit residential dwelling or a unit in a condominium complex or a PUD owned by an individual who does not occupy the dwelling. The dwelling is leased and occupied as a principal year-round residence to individuals other than the owner.” \[G §3.41, p. 11\]

STD-1.3 The Program Summary is listed as “Business Purpose DSCR” on Acra's rate-sheet page. “Where the borrower is qualifying utilizing the subject property's actual or market cashflow under a business purpose transaction, borrower must execute with loan docs a Business Purpose Attestation (Exhibit 8) or other similar attestation approved by Acra.” The excerpt's §8.4 also refers to consumer transactions (STD-9.2); whether every loan on this program is a business-purpose transaction: Acra confirmation requested → Q-27. \[G §5.32, p. 3; acralending.com/ratesheets\]

STD-1.4 The matrix columns are Purchase, Rate & Term and Cash-Out. Delayed financing is addressed only by the matrix footnote “Delayed financing is capped at \$1.5MM”. Which column and which cash-in-hand rule apply to delayed financing: Acra confirmation requested → Q-06. \[S: matrix and footnote\]

STD-1.5 A loan qualifies either by a calculated DSCR (§5.32) or as No Ratio DSCR, where no ratio is calculated (§5.33). Both are set out in section 3. \[G §5.32–5.33, p. 3\]

STD-1.6 “Borrowing entity income documentation not required.” Acra will not calculate a DTI for applicants who qualify using a DSCR; income or employment listed on an application is superfluous to the underwrite and may be left blank, and if represented, a DTI should not be calculated. \[S: Income Documentation; G §7.3, p. 5\]

rule.description: Determine whether the loan uses a calculated DSCR or No Ratio DSCR qualification method.

ledger.clause:
1.1 Occupancy, purpose and qualification
STD-1.1 Occupancy is investment property (non-owner occupied) only. \[S: Occupancy Type\]

STD-1.2 An investment property is “a one- to four-unit residential dwelling or a unit in a condominium complex or a PUD owned by an individual who does not occupy the dwelling. The dwelling is leased and occupied as a principal year-round residence to individuals other than the owner.” \[G §3.41, p. 11\]

STD-1.3 The Program Summary is listed as “Business Purpose DSCR” on Acra's rate-sheet page. “Where the borrower is qualifying utilizing the subject property's actual or market cashflow under a business purpose transaction, borrower must execute with loan docs a Business Purpose Attestation (Exhibit 8) or other similar attestation approved by Acra.” The excerpt's §8.4 also refers to consumer transactions (STD-9.2); whether every loan on this program is a business-purpose transaction: Acra confirmation requested → Q-27. \[G §5.32, p. 3; acralending.com/ratesheets\]

STD-1.4 The matrix columns are Purchase, Rate & Term and Cash-Out. Delayed financing is addressed only by the matrix footnote “Delayed financing is capped at \$1.5MM”. Which column and which cash-in-hand rule apply to delayed financing: Acra confirmation requested → Q-06. \[S: matrix and footnote\]

STD-1.5 A loan qualifies either by a calculated DSCR (§5.32) or as No Ratio DSCR, where no ratio is calculated (§5.33). Both are set out in section 3. \[G §5.32–5.33, p. 3\]

STD-1.6 “Borrowing entity income documentation not required.” Acra will not calculate a DTI for applicants who qualify using a DSCR; income or employment listed on an application is superfluous to the underwrite and may be left blank, and if represented, a DTI should not be calculated. \[S: Income Documentation; G §7.3, p. 5\]

PLAT-7.6 A property is considered listed for sale under §11.5 if it has been listed for sale in the last six months, measured from (a) the last date of being listed to (b) the Application Date. \[G §11.5, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.1 Gift funds, investment property: applicant(s) are required to contribute a portion of their own sourced and seasoned funds to the transaction at a minimum of 10% of the purchase price (PLAT-1.15). \[G §8.7, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.2 Verification of the seasoning of funds to close is required on loans over 70% CLTV for consumer transactions, or business purpose loans where funds to close are over \$50,000 and over 70% CLTV. Whether any loan on this program is a consumer transaction is Q-22. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.3 Where the account(s) serving as the source of funds must be verified, verification may include a copy of the borrower's bank statement(s) for the most recent month(s), or a VOD reflecting a current and average balance for the most recent month(s). \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.4 “All transactions require a minimum of 30-days documentation.” Whether any seasoning period applies to domestic funds beyond this documentation minimum: Acra confirmation requested → Q-11. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.5 “In contrast to the above, but consistent with §3.10.1 of this Guide, funds held in a foreign bank / currency will need to be repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing”. Foreign nationals are not eligible for this program, but an eligible US citizen or permanent resident may hold funds abroad; the same sentence's 60-day seasoning requirement is stated for Foreign Nationals only and is not restated. Whether the repatriation requirement applies to eligible borrowers holding funds abroad, and what evidence and timing convention apply: Acra confirmation requested → Q-11. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.6 “See guidelines for unacceptable source of funds” — the Seller's Guide provision is not reproduced (Appendix B). \[P: Reserve Requirements\]

ledger.clause:
PLAT-8.7 The sources state reserves only for the situations below and state the payment basis in none of them. The base requirement at CLTV of 75.00% or below, the payment basis (including on an interest-only loan), permitted sources, whether overlapping triggers are cumulative, and whether reserves substituted for rent loss insurance are additional: Acra confirmation requested → Q-08. \[P; G\]

| **Trigger** | **Reserves as printed** | **Source** |
|----|----|----|
| CLTV \> 75.00% | “6-months Reserves required for CLTV \> 75.00%” | P: Reserve Requirements |
| Property listed for sale within six months | Twenty-four (24) months of reserves; cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide | G §11.5 |
| Forbearance or mortgage lates in the last 12 months, tenant-occupied subject, without timely receipt of the prior two months' rent (relationship to 0x30x12: PLAT-3.12, Q-17) | 12 months of the subject's payment in reserve, which may be from the transaction's cash-in-hand | G §5.32 |
| Rent loss insurance required but cannot be obtained | Two (2) months reserves for every one (1) month of coverage not provided | G §23.40 |

condition.purpose: Determine whether the reserves requirement for the specified tenant-occupied subject condition is met.

PLAT-8.1 Gift funds, investment property: applicant(s) are required to contribute a portion of their own sourced and seasoned funds to the transaction at a minimum of 10% of the purchase price (PLAT-1.15). \[G §8.7, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.2 Verification of the seasoning of funds to close is required on loans over 70% CLTV for consumer transactions, or business purpose loans where funds to close are over \$50,000 and over 70% CLTV. Whether any loan on this program is a consumer transaction is Q-22. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.3 Where the account(s) serving as the source of funds must be verified, verification may include a copy of the borrower's bank statement(s) for the most recent month(s), or a VOD reflecting a current and average balance for the most recent month(s). \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.4 “All transactions require a minimum of 30-days documentation.” Whether any seasoning period applies to domestic funds beyond this documentation minimum: Acra confirmation requested → Q-11. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.5 “In contrast to the above, but consistent with §3.10.1 of this Guide, funds held in a foreign bank / currency will need to be repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing”. Foreign nationals are not eligible for this program, but an eligible US citizen or permanent resident may hold funds abroad; the same sentence's 60-day seasoning requirement is stated for Foreign Nationals only and is not restated. Whether the repatriation requirement applies to eligible borrowers holding funds abroad, and what evidence and timing convention apply: Acra confirmation requested → Q-11. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.6 “See guidelines for unacceptable source of funds” — the Seller's Guide provision is not reproduced (Appendix B). \[P: Reserve Requirements\]

ledger.clause:
5.1 Entity eligibility and guarantees
PLAT-5.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

condition.purpose: Verify that the required entity documents are provided and meet the stated content and validity requirements.
steps: Initial Document Review: Obtain and review a complete, legible Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments. Review the complete Operating Agreement for LLCs and Partnerships, or Bylaws for corporations, with all referenced exhibits and amendments. Verify it states whether the entity is member or manager managed, contains authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers. Review all documentation evidencing ownership interests. For S or C Corporations, review compliant shareholder / stockholder certificates or, if lost or unavailable, the stock ledger; if stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable, review an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate. For S-corporations or Partnerships where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable, review the most recent preceding tax year's K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest and a CPA or Tax Preparer letter affirming current ownership interest, with a statement to that effect if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed.

Eligibility Verification: Verify that names on entity documents match the identification or, if they do not match exactly, that a letter of explanation addresses the discrepancy. Verify a Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document is valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date. If the entity is formed in a state other than where business is being conducted or where the property is located, verify a Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the applicable state. Verify IRS Form SS4 or a Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter. An EIN exception request may be submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds. Review a Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest, authorizing the transaction with Acra Lending and identifying who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity. Verify any Power of Attorney utilized to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee meets the stated reference to §23.5(C).

Validation and Verification: Do not accept a borrower letter stating that a required document is not required, available, or excused. Refer conflicts between formation documents and the Operating Agreement or Bylaws for additional information. Note that a Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution cannot be used to designate a signor on a personal guarantee. Address additional supporting documentation if Legal conditions for it in its sole discretion.
Final Determination: Record whether the required entity documentation is complete and meets the stated requirements, including any additional supporting documentation condition.
checks: The required entity documents are provided, complete, legible where required, and meet the stated content, ownership, signature, and validity requirements; no borrower letter is used to excuse a required document.

outcomes.criterion: All required entity documentation is provided and meets the stated requirements, with no outstanding condition.

ledger.clause:
5.2 Entity documentation
PLAT-5.10 The documents below are required, without exception, and borrower letters stating that they are not required, available, or excused from providing such documents are not acceptable. \[G §3.12, pp. 8–9\]

- Complete, legible copy of the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments thereto.

- Complete (with all referenced exhibits), legible copy of the Operating Agreement for LLCs and Partnerships, or Bylaws for corporations, and all amendments, that states whether the entity is member or manager managed, contains authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers. Additional information may be required if the formation documents and the Operating Agreement or Bylaws conflict.

- All documentation evidencing ownership interests: for LLCs and Partnerships, the Operating Agreement must identify, or attach as an exhibit, all persons by name with their ownership interest, or provide copies of the membership interest certificates / units in compliance with the Operating Agreement.

- For S or C Corporations: shareholder / stockholder certificates that comply with the Bylaws, if any, or, if stock certificates are lost or unavailable, the corporation's stock ledger. - Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date.

ledger.clause:
5.1 Entity eligibility and guarantees
PLAT-5.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]
