ledger.clause:
5.1 Entity eligibility and guarantees
PLAT-5.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust meets all stated requirements.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the title commitment and a complete, legible copy of the Trust or a Certification of Trust. Verify that the Certification states the existence and date of the Trust; the Trustor(s) and current Trustee(s); the powers of the Trustee; whether the Trust is revocable and, if revocable, who holds the right to revoke; the names and number of Trustees required to sign on behalf of the Trust; the Trust identification number (a Social Security number or an IRS-issued Tax Identification Number); how title to the Trust assets should be taken; and that the Trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner.

Eligibility Verification: Verify that the Trust is valid under the laws of the state in which it is established; is revocable and can be changed or canceled at any time for any reason during a Trustor's lifetime; is established by one or more natural persons, solely or jointly, and becomes effective during their lifetime; and has the individual(s) establishing it as its primary beneficiary.

Validation and Verification: Verify that written exception by Acra Senior Management is obtained if the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same. Verify that the Trust specifies the Trustee's power to hold title and mortgage the property; that the beneficiary does not need to grant written consent for the Trust to borrow money, or that such consent has been granted in writing for purposes of the mortgage; that there is no unusual risk or impairment to the lender's rights; and that holding title in the Trust does not diminish the lender's rights as a creditor. Address additional supporting documentation if Legal conditions for it in its sole discretion.
Final Determination: Record whether every stated trust-title requirement is met and whether any additional supporting documentation condition remains.
checks: The inter vivos revocable Trust meets all stated documentation, validity, revocability, establishment, beneficiary, exception, power, consent, risk, and lender-rights requirements.

outcomes.criterion: Every stated trust-title requirement is met, with no outstanding condition.
The requirements are met subject to any required written exception or additional supporting documentation condition being obtained or cleared.
A stated trust-title requirement is not met.
Title is not vested in an inter vivos revocable trust.

ledger.clause:
PLAT-5.13 Title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust is permitted when all of the following requirements are followed. \[G §3.12, pp. 9–10\]

- A complete, legible copy of the Trust, or a Certification of Trust stating: the existence and date of the Trust; the Trustor(s) and the current Trustee(s); the powers of the Trustee; whether the Trust is revocable and, if revocable, who holds the right to revoke; the names and number of the Trustees required to sign on behalf of the Trust; the Trust identification number (a Social Security number or an IRS-issued Tax Identification Number); how title to the Trust assets should be taken; and a statement that the Trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner.

- The Trust must be valid under the laws of the state in which it is established.

- The Trust must be revocable, meaning it can be changed or canceled at any time for any reason during a Trustor's lifetime. Irrevocable trust is not permitted.

- The Trust must be established by one or more natural persons, solely or jointly (Grantor, Trustor, or Settlor), and must become effective during the lifetime of the person(s) establishing it.

- The primary beneficiary of the Trust must be the individual(s) establishing the Trust.

- Written exception by Acra Senior Management must be obtained if the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same.

- The Trust must specify that the Trustee has the power to hold title and mortgage the property; that the beneficiary does not need to grant written consent for the Trust to borrow money, or that such consent has been granted in writing for purposes of the mortgage; that there is no unusual risk or impairment to the lender's rights; and that holding title in the Trust does not diminish the lender's rights as a creditor.

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

For loans that close in the name of an entity, use the highest middle score of the personal guarantors, presuming equal percentages of ownership. If ownership percentages differ, use the individual with the highest concentration of ownership.” \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements\]

PLAT-6.2 Minimum decisioning score 700 (no matrix row below 700, PLAT-2.1); Correspondent pricing limited to 60% CLTV for 700-719 (PLAT-2.3). \[P: matrix; footnote 3\]

PLAT-6.3 “Tradelines: Applicants with scores from 3 repositories are deemed to be acceptable with no tradeline overlay. 2 tradelines & 24 month history or 3 tradelines & 12 month history for applicants with 2 or fewer scores.” \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements\]

PLAT-6.4 Applicants with one score are within “2 or fewer scores” for the tradeline requirement above. The Platinum Summary does not state how the decisioning score is set with one score or with two scores, whether any no-score pathway exists, or how “Primary Wage Earner” is identified on a file with no income documentation. The Standard Summary's one-or-no-score provision is not restated here: Acra confirmation requested → Q-05. \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements\]

PLAT-6.5 Where two or more guarantors hold an equal largest ownership interest and ownership is not equal across all guarantors, PLAT-6.1 does not say whose score is used: Acra confirmation requested → Q-05. \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements\]

condition.purpose: Establish the decisioning credit score used for the loan.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the credit report for the applicable borrower’s or personal guarantors’ scores; for an entity loan, review entity documents and ownership information to identify guarantors and their ownership percentages.

Final Determination: Record the decisioning credit score established under PLAT-6.1, or record that the source does not resolve the applicable selection.

PLAT-6.1 “Decisioning Credit Score: Primary Wage Earner middle score. For loans that close in the name of an entity, use the highest middle score of the personal guarantors, presuming equal percentages of ownership. rule.description: Determine whether the borrower's citizenship status is one of the eligible types.

ledger.clause:
The Platinum Summary lists two eligible citizenship types and excludes first-time homebuyers. Borrowing entities, guarantors and trusts follow the Seller's Guide excerpt and are in section 5.

PLAT-4.1 Eligible borrower citizenship types: US Citizen, Permanent Resident. \[P: Borrower Citizenship Requirements\]

PLAT-4.2 Permanent Resident must have an unexpired PRA ID and SSA card / SSA-89. \[P: Borrower Citizenship Requirements\]

PLAT-4.3 Non-permanent residents, foreign nationals and ITIN borrowers are not among the listed eligible types. The Seller's Guide foreign-national program (§3.10) is therefore not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Borrower Citizenship Requirements\]

PLAT-4.4 “First Time Homebuyer (FTHB) ineligible for this program”. Acra defines a First Time Home Buyer as “an application where all Applicants have never previously owned a home (real property)”; the §3.13 DSCR allowance for first-time homebuyers is not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements; G §3.13, p. 10\]

PLAT-4.5 §3.12 requires at least one guarantor to have prior homeownership experience, and at least one borrower / guarantor to attest on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer (PLAT-5.9). Whether it applies to individual borrowers as well as entities is part of Q-13. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

ledger.clause:
1.1 Occupancy, purpose and qualification
PLAT-1.7 The program is offered through two channels with different minimum ratios: Correspondent ≥ 1.2, Wholesale ≥ 1.0 (PLAT-3.7). Matrix footnote 3 also restricts Correspondent pricing (PLAT-2.3). \[P: Minimum DSCR; matrix footnote 3\]

PLAT-1.8 Every loan must meet the applicable channel minimum DSCR. The Platinum Summary lists no No Ratio option and no allowance for a ratio below 1.0; a ratio below the channel minimum does not meet the published requirement. Whether No Ratio or sub-1.0 qualification exists on this program in any form: Acra confirmation requested → Q-12. \[P: Minimum DSCR\]

PLAT-1.9 Acra will not calculate a DTI for applicants who qualify using a DSCR; income or employment listed on an application is superfluous to the underwrite and may be left blank, and if represented, a DTI should not be calculated. The Standard Summary's statement that borrowing-entity income documentation is not required does not appear in the Platinum Summary; whether it applies: Acra confirmation requested → Q-13. \[G §7.3, p. 5\]

PLAT-1.10 “A 1007 will always be required on DSCR transactions”; the Platinum Summary refers to market rent “as established on the 1007 or 1025”. Whether a Form 1025 alone satisfies the requirement for a two-unit property: Acra confirmation requested → Q-04. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §14.12, p. 4; P: Income Documentation\]

PLAT-1.11 All borrowers purchasing or refinancing a one- to four-family investment property must execute a One- to Four-Family Rider with the loan documents and provide rent loss insurance coverage per §23.40 (PLAT-7.9 to 7.12). \[G §3.41, p. 11\]

PLAT-1.12 Only the subject property, principal residence and second homes are required to be listed on the application or Schedule of Real Estate Owned. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §4.15, p. 5\]

PLAT-3.7 Minimum Debt Service Coverage Ratio: Correspondent ≥ 1.2; Wholesale ≥ 1.0. \[P: Minimum DSCR\]

PLAT-3.8 Property listed for sale within six months (§11.5): the excerpt requires “≥1.0 DSCR”; on this program the channel minimum applies — Wholesale 1.0, Correspondent 1.2 (PLAT-7.8). \[G §11.5, p. 11; P: Minimum DSCR\]

ledger.clause:
PLAT-3.1 “When calculating the DSCR, Acra will use the greater of the market rent as established on the 1007 or 1025, or actual rent. When using actual rent, the actual rent must be documented via evidence of 2 months’ proof of receipts and the lease must be in place for at least 3 months after the loan closing. This applies to long-term rents only and is not appropriate for short-term rentals.” \[P: Income Documentation & Debt Ratio Requirements\]

PLAT-3.2 §5.32 of the excerpt states the general formula as “the lesser of (i) annual in-place rent or (ii) market rent”, then notes that “Acra may use the higher of actual or market rents” subject to “two (2) consecutive months proof of rental income receipt”, a lease continuing at least three months after closing, and: “Security Deposit does not count towards receipt, and the rents cannot be prepaid.” The Platinum Summary's statement (PLAT-3.1) is program-specific; the excerpt's general formula is reproduced here. Which governs Platinum Select and how they relate, whether “2 months’ proof of receipts” means consecutive months, and whether the security-deposit and prepaid-rent conditions apply: Acra confirmation requested → Q-03. \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

PLAT-3.3 Short-term rentals are ineligible for the program (PLAT-7.2); the Seller's Guide provisions on short-term rental income and appraisal forms are not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Subject Property Requirements\]

Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Establish whether the subject property is a one- to four-unit, non-owner occupied income property and whether subject property rents are used to qualify.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Verify the loan-to-value (LTV) and compare it with 70%; compare the case-field CLTV with 70%. If LTV is at or below 70% while CLTV is above 70%, request Acra confirmation.

Step 4 - Final Determination: Determine whether rent loss insurance is required, applying the stated requirement and CLTV exemption, and leave the determination pending Acra confirmation for the stated LTV/CLTV case.
checks: The subject property is a one- to four-unit, non-owner occupied income property.
The subject property's LTV is greater than 70%.
Subject property rents are used to qualify.
LoanCore.cltv_percent is at or below 70%.
The subject property's LTV is at or below 70% and LoanCore.cltv_percent is above 70%.

outcomes.criterion: The property conditions, LTV, rent-use condition, and CLTV treatment establish that rent loss insurance is required.
LTV is at or below 70% and CLTV is above 70%; Acra confirmation has been requested and the determination remains pending.
There is no case for this outcome.
The policy conditions requiring rent loss insurance do not apply, including when CLTV is at or below 70%.

ledger.clause:
PLAT-7.9 Rent loss insurance covers rental losses that are incurred during the period that a property is being rehabilitated following a casualty. \[G §23.40, p. 13\]

PLAT-7.10 Six (6) months' rent loss insurance is required on one- to four-unit non-owner occupied income properties with LTV \> 70% and when subject property rents are used to qualify. \[G §23.40, p. 13\]

PLAT-7.11 “Loans with ≤ 70% CLTV are not required to carry rent loss insurance.” The requirement is stated in LTV and the exemption in CLTV; the case of LTV at or below 70% with CLTV above 70%: Acra confirmation requested → Q-10. \[G §23.40, p. 13\]

PLAT-7.12 When rent loss insurance is required but cannot be obtained, the borrower may substitute two (2) months reserves for every one (1) month of rent loss coverage not provided. \[G §23.40, p. 13\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the required rent loss protection is provided through six (6) months' coverage or the allowed reserve substitution.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the hazard insurance declarations and bank statement for evidence of rent loss coverage and reserves.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Confirm that the Rent Loss Insurance Requirement determination applies to the case; if it does not apply, this job is not applicable.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Verify that the insurance covers rental losses incurred during the period the property is being rehabilitated following a casualty. If required coverage cannot be obtained, verify the months of coverage not provided and the available reserves against the substitution requirement of two (2) months reserves for every one (1) month of rent loss coverage not provided.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Determine whether six (6) months' rent loss insurance is provided or, when it cannot be obtained, the required reserve substitution is met.

The rent loss insurance covers rental losses incurred during the period the property is being rehabilitated following a casualty.
Six (6) months' rent loss insurance is provided.
When required rent loss insurance cannot be obtained, reserves equal two (2) months for every one (1) month of rent loss coverage not provided are available.

condition.purpose: Determine whether the product and any interest-only feature meet the stated program requirements.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the loan application for product type, ARM terms, and interest-only terms.

Eligibility Verification: Verify that the product is 30 Yr Fixed, 5 Yr ARM, 30 Yr Fixed Interest-Only, or 5 Yr ARM Interest-Only. For an ARM, verify Index 1 Yr CMT, Caps 2/2/6, and the stated margin by FICO. For interest-only, verify the 5 Yr Term and the maximum CLTV of 75.00%.
Validation and Verification: Confirm the product and terms against the loan application and case record; verify that interest-only is not used on a property listed for sale.
Final Determination: Record whether the product and applicable restrictions are met.
checks: The product is 30 Yr Fixed, 5 Yr ARM, 30 Yr Fixed Interest-Only, or 5 Yr ARM Interest-Only.
If the product is an ARM, its index is 1 Yr CMT and its caps are 2/2/6.
If the product is an ARM, its margin is 3.00 for FICO 760+, 3.25 for FICO 720-759, or 3.50 for FICO 700-719.
If the loan is interest-only, it has a 5 Yr Term and CLTV is no more than 75.00%.
If the loan is interest-only, the property is not listed for sale.

outcomes.criterion: Every applicable product and interest-only check holds.
There is no case for this outcome.
An applicable product or interest-only check does not hold.
There is no case for this outcome.

missing_reads: Product type, ARM index, ARM caps, ARM margin, and interest-only term, if not established in the case record.
Acra confirmation regarding whether a minimum loan amount or minimum FICO applies to interest-only loans.

rule.description: Verify that the product is listed as eligible and that interest-only restrictions are met.

ledger.clause:
PLAT-9.1 Eligible product types: 30 Yr Fixed, 5 Yr ARM, 30 Yr Fixed Interest-Only, 5 Yr ARM Interest-Only. \[P: Product Requirements\]

PLAT-9.2 ARM requirements: Index 1 Yr CMT; Caps 2/2/6; Margin 3.00 (FICO 760+), 3.25 (FICO 720-759), 3.50 (FICO 700-719). \[P: ARM Requirements\]

PLAT-9.3 “Interest-Only (5 Yr Term), Max CLTV: 75.00%”. \[P: Product Requirements — Restrictions\]

PLAT-9.4 No minimum loan amount or minimum FICO is printed for interest-only loans on Platinum Select: Acra confirmation requested → Q-09. \[P: Product Requirements\]

PLAT-9.5 Interest-only is not available on a property listed for sale (PLAT-7.8). \[G §11.5, p. 11\]

PLAT-9.6 Interest Only payments are calculated as the amount sufficient to pay the accrued interest on the mortgage monthly at the time of origination, usually for a set term at the beginning of the repayment term; after that term the payments are recast to a fully amortized payment for the balance of the term ending at maturity. Acra calculates the DSCR using the first payment due under the Note (PLAT-3.5; which payment enters the denominator on an interest-only loan is Q-21). The excerpt's DTI calculation for interest-only loans is a DTI-program provision — Q-14. \[G §7.5, p. 13\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the loan meets the stated CLTV caps for the applicable loan amount, property type, interest-only term, or listing history.

If the property was listed for sale within six months, CLTV is no more than 65%.
If FICO is 730 and above, CLTV is no more than 80% for Purchase, 80% for Rate & Term, or 75% for Cash-Out.

SOURCE CLAUSE:
STD-8.1 Eligible property types: SFR, Townhome, PUD, Warrantable Condo, Non-Warrantable Condo, Condotel / PUDtel, 2-4 Units, Manufactured. Restrictions as printed: \[S: Subject Property Type\]

| **Property type** | **Purchase** | **Refi R/T** | **Refi C/O** | **Conditions as printed** |
|----|----|----|----|----|
| Non-Warrantable Condo | 80% | 75% | 75% | “-5% CLTV for Florida properties, Min DSCR: 1.0” |
| Condotel / PUDtel | 75% | 70% | 65% | “-5% CLTV for Florida properties Min DSCR: 1.0” |
| 2-4 Unit | 80% | 80% | 80% | Printed as “Max CLTV: 80%” with no purpose split |
| Manufactured Home | 65% | 60% | 60% | — |

STD-8.2 Above 80.00% LTV only SFR, Warrantable Condos outside of Florida, Townhome and PUD are eligible (STD-3.16). \[S: Income Documentation\]

STD-8.3 Rural / unique property: maximum CLTV 80% (purchase), 75% (refinance — rate & term), 70% (refinance — cash-out); minimum FICO 700; minimum DSCR 1.00. “If marketing time is excessive or property exhibits unusual, inadequate or peculiar functionality, LTV may be further reduced.” \[S: Subject Property Location\]

condition.source:
import rules_lib

def check(ctx):
    property_type = ctx['SubjectProperty.property_type']
    missing = rules_lib.gaps(property_type=property_type)
    if missing:
        return rules_lib.unknown(*missing)
    return rules_lib.same(
        property_type,
        'SFR',
        'Townhome',
        'PUD',
        'Warrantable Condo',
        'Non-Warrantable Condo',
        'Condotel / PUDtel',
        '2-4 Units',
        'Manufactured',
    )

evidence.excerpt:
SKILL: Check the stated loan conditions for a property listed for sale under §11.5.
PURPOSE: Determine whether a loan on a property listed for sale meets the characteristics stated in §11.5.
CHECKS TO ENCODE:
  - If the property is considered listed for sale and is an investment property, the subject is occupied by a tenant and is not vacant.
  - If the property is considered listed for sale, reserves are 24 months; cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide.
  - If the property is considered listed for sale, the loan has a fully amortizing term and is not interest only.
CHECKS LEFT TO A REVIEWER:
  - If the property is considered listed for sale, the property is not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s).
  - If the property is considered listed for sale, the loan qualifies as either at least 1.0 DSCR or 43% maximum DTI.
  - If the property is considered listed for sale, the prepayment penalty is at least three years unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties.
  - If the property is considered listed for sale, maximum LTV / CLTV is 65% based on the lesser of appraised value or lowest recent listing price.
  - If the property is considered listed for sale, there is no subordinate financing.
  - If the property is considered listed for sale, impounds are in place.
SOURCE CLAUSE:
STD-8.8 A property is considered listed for sale under §11.5 if it has been listed for sale in the last six months, measured from (a) the last date of being listed to (b) the Application Date. \[G §11.5, p. 12\]

STD-8.9 Loans on such properties will be considered under the following characteristics: the property is not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s); for investment properties, the subject must be occupied by a tenant and may not be vacant; the loan must qualify as either (a) ≥ 1.0 DSCR or (b) 43% maximum DTI (Q-14); a prepayment penalty of at least three (3) years is required unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties; twenty-four (24) months of reserves are required, and cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide; the loan must have a fully amortizing term, interest only is not available; the maximum LTV / CLTV is 65% based on the lesser of (a) appraised value or (b) lowest recent listing price; no subordinate financing is allowed; impounds are required. \[G §11.5, pp. 11–12\]

proposals.reasoning: The source clause defines listed-for-sale status as a property listed in the last six months; the supplied last-six-months field is used as that determination. For such properties, the function checks the 24 months of reserves and that the loan is not interest only. For investment properties it also requires a current tenant lease and that the property is not vacant. Cash-in-hand is permissive rather than a required condition, and the other checks are left to the reviewer.

evidence.excerpt:
SKILL: Check the stated cash-out refinance conditions for a vacant property and flag matters requiring Acra confirmation.
PURPOSE: Determine whether a vacant property cash-out refinance meets the conditions stated in the Summary.
CHECKS TO ENCODE:
  - If the property is vacant and the transaction is a cash-out refinance, no interest-only program is used.
  - If the property is vacant and the transaction is a cash-out refinance, reserves are at least six months.
  - If the property is vacant and the transaction is a cash-out refinance with a loan amount under $1,500,000, CLTV is no more than 60%.
CHECKS LEFT TO A REVIEWER:
  - If the property is vacant and the transaction is a cash-out refinance, the minimum FICO score is 700.
  - If the property is vacant and the transaction is a cash-out refinance, DSCR is at least 1.15.
  - If the property is vacant and the transaction is a cash-out refinance, the prepayment penalty is at least three years where allowable.
  - If the property is vacant and the transaction is a cash-out refinance, impounds are in place.
  - If the property is vacant and the transaction is a cash-out refinance, ownership is at least 15 months.
  - If the property is vacant and the transaction is a cash-out refinance with a loan amount of $1,500,000 or more, Acra confirmation is obtained.
  - If the property is vacant and the transaction is a cash-out refinance, Acra confirmation is obtained on how the 15 months of ownership are measured.
SOURCE CLAUSE:
STD-8.5 A vacant property may be purchased; qualifying rents are taken from the 1007 or 1025 (STD-3.8). “Vacant investment properties are only eligible for a refinance transaction if consistent with §10.17.” \[G §5.32, p. 3; §3.41, p. 11\]

STD-8.6 Rate and term refinance of a vacant property (§10.17): minimum 700 FICO score; maximum \$1,000,000 to maximum 70% CLTV; maximum \$2,000,000 to maximum 65% CLTV; minimum 1.000 DSCR or maximum 40.0% DTI (Q-14); minimum two-year prepayment penalty (where allowable); full amortization required, no interest-only programs; impounds required; minimum six months reserves. The Summary states the same conditions with “Max CLTV 70% for loan amounts under \$1,000,000 and 65% for loan amounts under \$2,000,000”. Treatment at exactly \$1,000,000 and \$2,000,000: Acra confirmation requested → Q-10. \[G §10.17, p. 11; S: Occupancy Type\]

STD-8.7 Cash-out refinance of a vacant property: the “Cash-Out Refinances” heading in §10.17 is empty in the excerpt. The Summary states: minimum 700 FICO; DSCR ≥ 1.15; ≥ 3-year PPP (where allowable); no interest only; impounds required; 6 months reserves; “Max CLTV 60% for loan amounts under \$1,500,000”; “Requires ≥15 months ownership”. Loans of \$1,500,000 or more, and how the 15 months are measured: Acra confirmation requested → Q-10. \[S: Occupancy Type; G §10.17, p. 11\]

proposals.reasoning: Applies only when the property is vacant and the loan purpose is cash-out refinance. Encodes the stated no-interest-only condition, at least 6 months of reserves, and the maximum 60% CLTV only for loan amounts under $1,500,000. At $1,500,000 or more, CLTV is not checked here; Acra confirmation and all other reviewer items are left out of the decision.

rule.description: Python formalization of acra-standard.asset_assessment_assets_and_funds_to_close.funds_to_close_seasoning_verification_trigger
citations: Acra_DSCR_Standard_Consolidated_Guidelines_v1_0.docx#9.1 Gift funds, funds to close and seasoning

evidence.excerpt:
SKILL: Determine whether the stated CLTV and transaction conditions require verification of funds-to-close seasoning.
PURPOSE: Determine whether STD-9.2 requires verification of seasoning of funds to close.
CHECKS (encode those the case fields settle; leave the rest to a reviewer):
  - For a consumer transaction, CLTV is over 70%.
  - For a business purpose loan, funds to close are over $50,000.
  - For a business purpose loan, CLTV is over 70%.
SOURCE CLAUSE:
STD-9.1 Gift funds, investment property or second homes: applicant(s) are required to contribute a portion of their own sourced and seasoned funds to the transaction at a minimum of 10% of the purchase price. Gift documentation requirements are in the Seller's Guide gift-fund section (Appendix B). \[G §8.7, p. 12; S: Loan Amount\]

STD-9.2 Verification of the seasoning of funds to close is required on loans over 70% CLTV for consumer transactions, or business purpose loans where funds to close are over \$50,000 and over 70% CLTV. Whether any loan on this program is a consumer transaction: Acra confirmation requested → Q-27. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.3 Where the account(s) serving as the source of funds must be verified, verification may include a copy of the borrower's bank statement(s) for the most recent month(s), or a VOD reflecting a current and average balance for the most recent month(s). \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.4 “All transactions require a minimum of 30-days documentation.” Whether any seasoning period applies to domestic funds beyond this documentation minimum: Acra confirmation requested → Q-12. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

condition.source:
import rules_lib

def check(ctx):
    entity_type = ctx['Borrower.entity_type']
    missing = rules_lib.gaps(entity_type=entity_type)
    if missing:
        return rules_lib.unknown(*missing)

    allowed = rules_lib.same(
        entity_type,
        'Domestic Corporation', 'Corporation', 'C Corp', 'S Corp',
        'Domestic C Corporation', 'Domestic S Corporation',
        'Limited Liability Company', 'LLC', 'Single Purpose LLC',
        'Limited Liability Partnership', 'LLP',
        'Limited Liability Limited Partnership', 'LLLP',
        'General Partnership', 'GP',
        'Limited Partnership', 'LP',
        'Sole Proprietorship'
    )
    return (bool(allowed), {'entity_type': entity_type})

rule.description: Python formalization of acra-standard.compliance_and_closing_the_borrowing_entity_and_title.entity_form_eligibility

evidence.excerpt:
SKILL: Verify that the entity or guarantor type and ownership structure are among those allowed by the guidelines.
PURPOSE: Determine whether the entity form and structure meet the stated eligibility requirements.
CHECKS (encode those the case fields settle; leave the rest to a reviewer):
  - The entity is US formed and based and is not a foreign entity or foreign owned entity.
  - The entity type is allowed and is not a type listed as not allowed.
  - Business entity nesting, if any, is limited to only one (1) wholly-owned subsidiary owned by individual(s), with no multiple nesting or ownership by multiple entities, trusts, etcetera.
SOURCE CLAUSE:
6.1 Entity eligibility and guarantees
STD-6.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

6.1 Entity eligibility and guarantees
STD-6.8 Not allowed: Cooperatives, Irrevocable Trusts, Land Trusts, IRAs, Non-Profit, and Joint Ventures. “Business entity nesting is limited to only one (1) wholly-owned subsidiary that in turn must be owned by individual(s); multiple nesting or ownership by multiple entities, trusts, etcetera are not acceptable.” An illustration of the permitted structure: Acra confirmation requested → Q-22. \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

STD-6.9 Acra requires at least one guarantor to have prior homeownership experience. At least one (1) borrower / guarantor on the loan must attest on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer; if prior home ownership is not evident within the loan file, the underwriter reserves the right to condition for supporting documentation. See Q-09. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

proposals.reasoning: The provided fields settle only the entity-type check, so the function uses the source's allowed entity-type categories as a whitelist; types not on that list, including the stated prohibited types, fail. No numeric threshold applies. The available fields do not establish US formation or base, foreign ownership, LLC single-purpose status beyond its stated type label, or the nesting and ownership structure, so those checks are left to a reviewer.

rule.description: Python formalization of acra-standard.compliance_and_closing_the_borrowing_entity_and_title.required_entity_documents

evidence.excerpt:
SKILL: Review the required entity documents and verify completeness against the guideline list; borrower letters claiming a document is not required, available, or excused do not satisfy the requirement.
PURPOSE: Determine whether the required entity documentation has been provided and meets the stated requirements.
CHECKS (encode those the case fields settle; leave the rest to a reviewer):
  - The complete, legible Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments thereto are provided.
  - The complete, legible Operating Agreement for LLCs and Partnerships, or Bylaws for corporations, with all referenced exhibits and amendments, is provided and states whether the entity is member or manager managed, contains authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers.
  - All required documentation evidencing ownership interests is provided, including the applicable ownership names and interests or membership interest certificates / units in compliance with the Operating Agreement.
  - For S or C Corporations, required shareholder / stockholder certificates or, if stock certificates are lost or unavailable, the stock ledger is provided and accounts for all outstanding shares noted in the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization, including those held by the corporation; an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate is provided if stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable.
  - For S-corporations or Partnerships where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable, the most recent preceding tax year's K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest and a letter from the CPA or Tax Preparer affirming current ownership interest are provided, with a statement to that effect if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed.
  - Names on the entity documents match the identification or a letter of explanation addresses the discrepancy.
  - A Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date is provided.
  - A Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted is provided if the entity is formed in a state other than where business is performed or where the property is located.
  - IRS Form SS4 or Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter is provided, unless an EIN exception request is submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds.
  - A Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest authorizes the transaction with Acra Lending and identifies who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity.
  - Any Power of Attorney used to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee is utilized by the principal.
  - No borrower letter is relied on to claim a required document is not required, available, or excused.
SOURCE CLAUSE:
6.2 Entity documentation
STD-6.10 The documents below are required, without exception, and borrower letters stating that they are not required, available, or excused from providing such documents are not acceptable. \[G §3.12, pp. 8–9\]

- Complete, legible copy of the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments thereto.

- Complete (with all referenced exhibits), legible copy of the Operating Agreement for LLCs and Partnerships, or Bylaws for corporations, and all amendments, that states whether the entity is member or manager managed, contains authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers. Additional information may be required if the formation documents and the Operating Agreement or Bylaws conflict.

- All documentation evidencing ownership interests: for LLCs and Partnerships, the Operating Agreement must identify, or attach as an exhibit, all persons by name with their ownership interest, or provide copies of the membership interest certificates / units in compliance with the Operating Agreement.

- For S or C Corporations: shareholder / stockholder certificates that comply with the Bylaws, if any, or, if stock certificates are lost or unavailable, the corporation's stock ledger. The certificate or ledger must account for all outstanding shares noted in the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization, including those held by the corporation. If stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable, an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate is required.

- For S-corporations or Partnerships, where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable: (i) the most recent preceding tax year's K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest, and (ii) a letter from the CPA or Tax Preparer affirming current ownership interest, with a statement to that effect if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed.

6.2 Entity documentation
- Names on the entity documents must match the identification; if they do not match exactly, a letter of explanation is required to address the discrepancy.

- Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date.

- Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted, if the entity is formed in a state other than where business is performed or where the property is located.

- IRS Form SS4 or Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter for the entity. EIN exception requests may be submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds.

- A Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest, (i) authorizing the transaction with Acra Lending and (ii) identifying who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity. It may be required by the Operating Agreement or Bylaws even where ownership is held by one individual. It cannot be used to designate a signor on a personal guarantee, only an authorized signor for the loan documents signed by the entity.

- A Power of Attorney must be utilized by the principal to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee; see §23.5(C), not reproduced (Appendix B).

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

proposals.reasoning: The available field directly indicates whether the required entity documents are complete. No field supplies the underlying documents, the circumstances for conditional requirements, or evidence of borrower letters, so those details cannot be assessed separately. In particular, the 20% ownership and ninety (90)-day requirements are left to a reviewer rather than inferred from unavailable fields.

CHECKS TO ENCODE:

  - An interest-only loan is not on a property listed for sale.
SOURCE CLAUSE:
STD-10.3 Interest Only, 5 Yr / 30 Year Fixed or 5/1 and 7/1 ARM: minimum loan ≥ \$250K; minimum 640 credit score. \[S: Product Requirements\]

STD-10.4 Interest Only, 10 Yr / 40 Year Term: minimum loan ≥ \$250K; minimum 640 credit score; maximum 80% LTV / CLTV; maximum \$3M loan amount. \[S: Product Requirements\]

STD-10.5 Interest-only is not available to first-time homebuyers (STD-4.10), on vacant-property refinances (STD-8.6 and 8.7) or on properties listed for sale (STD-8.9). \[G §3.13, §10.17, §11.5\]

STD-10.6 Interest Only payments are calculated as the amount sufficient to pay the accrued interest on the mortgage monthly at the time of origination, usually for a set term at the beginning of the repayment term; after that term the payments are recast to a fully amortized payment for the balance of the term ending at maturity. Acra calculates the DSCR using the first payment due under the Note (STD-3.2; which payment enters the denominator on an interest-only loan is Q-26). The excerpt's DTI calculation for interest-only loans (first fully amortized payment on the original balance; for an ARM, the highest achievable rate at that payment's due date) is a DTI-program provision — Q-14. \[G §7.5, p. 13\]

proposals.reasoning: Implements only the three stated exclusions: first-time homebuyer, vacant-property refinance, and property listed for sale. No numeric thresholds apply. The refinance purpose matters only when the property is vacant.

condition.source:
import rules_lib

def check(ctx):
    interest_only = rules_lib.flag(ctx['MortgageLoanInformation.is_interest_only'])
    interest_only_10_40 = rules_lib.flag(ctx['LoanCore.is_interest_only_10_40'])
    loan_amount = ctx['LoanCore.total_loan_amount_usd']
    credit_score = ctx['CreditReport.representative_score']
    cltv = ctx['LoanCore.cltv_percent']

    missing = rules_lib.gaps(
        interest_only=interest_only,
        interest_only_10_40=interest_only_10_40,
        loan_amount=loan_amount,
        credit_score=credit_score,
        cltv=cltv,
    )
    if missing:
        return rules_lib.unknown(*missing)

    if interest_only and (loan_amount < 250000 or loan_amount > 3000000 or credit_score < 640):
        return False
    if interest_only and interest_only_10_40 and cltv > 80:
        return False
    return True
